deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the introduction to Riemann's student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation' (dated 1847, published posthumously in the Gesammelte Werke, 1876). It contains no formulas or derivations. It only sets out method and motivation.

(a) The results of ordinary differential and integral calculus are assumed. Riemann says he will not simply extend to fractional orders the results that hold for integer-order derivatives and integrals. Instead those integer-order results serve two purposes: to justify ('Begründung') the general operation announced on fol. 1, and as a guide ('Wegweiser') for finding it.

(b) For the second purpose he looks at the sequence of derivatives z, z', z'', ... The usual definition builds each derivative from the previous one by a recursive law, D^{n+1}z = d/dx (D^n z). That definition cannot reach members of the sequence with non-integer index. So an independent characterization of D^n z is needed.

(c) He proposes the Taylor expansion of z(x+h) in nonnegative integer powers of the increment h. This is carried out on the next page, eq. (1): z(x+h) = sum_{p>=0} h^p/p! * d^p z/dx^p. The coefficients are uniquely determined, so one may define D^n z as n! times the coefficient of h^n.

My note on what comes next (not on this page): Riemann then interpolates the index n to arbitrary real values. This leads to his generalized operation, essentially the Riemann–Liouville fractional integral plus complementary terms.

Nothing is computed on this page.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page; it contains no derivations.

Implicit assumption, made explicit on the next page: the expansion is taken as valid for every h. That requires z to be analytic (entire, if literally 'for every value of h'), which Riemann does not justify.

results.what: Program: define derivatives of arbitrary order by finding a non-recursive characterization of the n-th derivative, namely via the Taylor coefficients of z(x+h), and then interpolating in n.
results.modern_name: Fractional calculus; motivating step toward the Riemann–Liouville differintegral
results.usually_credited_to: Liouville (1832–37), Riemann (1847, publ. 1876); earlier ideas from Leibniz, Euler, Lacroix and Abel

results.what: Characterization of the n-th derivative as n! times the coefficient of h^n in the Taylor expansion of z(x+h).
results.usually_credited_to: Taylor (1715), Lagrange (derivatives defined via Taylor coefficients, 1797)

deep.surprise_reason: This page belongs to Riemann's well-known 1847 essay on fractional differentiation and integration, published in his Werke in 1876. It is purely introductory prose with no new mathematics. The Taylor-coefficient definition of the derivative is Lagrangian and standard.

checkable.asserts: The n-th derivative equals n! times the coefficient of h^n in z(x+h) (polynomial test case).
The same Taylor-coefficient characterization holds for an analytic non-polynomial function.

transcription_corrections: 'auf ihr erkanntes[?] Bildungsgesetz' should most likely read 'auf ihr recurrirendes Bildungsgesetz'. This fits the image and the sense: the recursive law of formation.
'nach einer andern[?] Bestimmung' should most likely read 'nach einer independenten Bestimmung' (an independent determination). This is consistent with the image.
'auch auf die die[?] gebr[ochenen][?] Ordnungen' is uncertain at the torn right edge; the sense is clearly 'fractional orders'.
'andern theils als[?] Wegweiser' fits the image as 'andern Theils als Wegweiser'; this is consistent with the sense.
